titleStmt.author: Ruusuvirta
Lipponen
Pellinen
Penttonen
Astikainen

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Auditory Cortical and Hippocampal-System Mismatch Responses to Duration Deviants in Urethane-Anesthetized Rats

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether mismatch responses to duration deviants appear in the hippocampal system at the same latency as in auditory cortex, or only later and secondarily
span.quote: Our interest was whether mismatch responses, whenever elicited, occupied both the auditory cortex and the hippocampus in a typical latency range of mismatch responses in urethane anesthetized rats or whether mismatch responses were only manifested in the auditory cortex and possibly only followed by later hippocampal activity.

span.label: is the received cortico-hippocampal division of labour — MMN cortical, P3a hippocampal — actually supported
span.quote: The evidence for this cortico-hippocampal dichotomy is scarce, however.

span.label: finds mismatch responses in auditory cortex and in three hippocampal sites at the same latency and in the same stimulus condition, which weakens the case for the hippocampus being merely downstream
span.quote: Most importantly, hippocampal and auditory cortical mismatch responses were found in the same latency range and in the same stimulus condition.

span.label: existence
span.quote: We found differential LFPs (mismatch responses) to duration deviant tones in the auditory cortex and in the hippocampal system (CA1, dentate gyrus, and subiculum) in urethane-anesthetized rats.

span.label: auditory mismatch responses to duration deviants
span.quote: The mismatch negativity (MMN) of event-related potentials (ERPs) reflects this initial stage of auditory change detection.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: In the present study, local-field potentials (LFPs) in urethane-anesthetized rats were recorded on the surface of the primary auditory cortex and in three locations of the hippocampal system (dentate gyrus, CA1, and subiculum, Figure 1 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A long standard-to-deviant interval lets the transient memory trace of the standard decay, so the deviant can no longer be registered as mismatching it, abolishing the response
span.quote: Secondly, the long (500-ms) SDI might have led to a high degree of degradation of the memory trace of the standard tone, preventing the detection of the deviant tone as not matching this trace [1] , [7] .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A short inter-deviant interval re-activates the mismatch generator too rapidly, diminishing the amplitude of the response it can produce
span.quote: First, the short inter-deviant interval (due to the 200-ms SSI) might have diminished mismatch responses by the fast-paced activation of their neural generator (in humans [43] – [45] , in cats [15] ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: In the responsive conditions the deviant differed from the standard on two features (duration and inter-stimulus interval) instead of one, making the change easier to detect
span.quote: The present pattern of observations may also reflect the fact that the deviant tone was distinguishable from the standard tone by two auditory features (tone duration and inter-stimulus interval) in the former pair of conditions as opposed to solely one feature (tone duration) in the latter pair [1] , [47] .

span.label: the animal analogue is given a deliberately looser definition than the human one, dropping the polarity requirement so a cross-species comparison is possible at all
span.quote: Mismatch responses (i.e., higher-amplitude brain responses to deviant tones than standard tones irrespectively of the polarity of these responses and despite these tones are only passively listened to)

span.label: that loosening turns out to be load-bearing rather than cautious: the cortical response is positive and the hippocampal one negative in the very same animals
span.quote: The responses - positive polarity in the auditory cortical and negative polarity in the hippocampal sites - appeared in the same latency range (between 51.5 and 89 ms post-change) and in all the recording sites, but only in the SSI 500 /SDI 200 -condition.

span.label: co-occurrence in latency and in condition is the argument against a downstream account — if the hippocampus were merely triggered by cortex it should lag
span.quote: This correspondence suggests that the hippocampal responses reflect the initial detection of deviant tones similarly to auditory cortical mismatch responses.

span.label: duration rather than frequency is chosen as the deviant feature specifically to avoid the refractoriness confound that a tonotopic dimension would introduce
span.quote: Sound frequency was not used due to its spatial coding from the cochlea [41] owing to a potential confounding effect of lower levels of refractoriness in afferent pathways activated by the rare deviant tone than the frequently occurring standard tones [1] .

span.label: two intervals are crossed so that the memory-trace account and the generator-refractoriness account make different predictions across the four cells
span.quote: Two standard-to-standard (SSI) and standard-to-deviant (SDI) intervals (200 ms vs. 500 ms) were applied in different combinations to vary the observability of responses resembling MMN (mismatch responses).

span.label: series order is counterbalanced across animals specifically because anesthetic depth drifts with time on the rig
span.quote: was counterbalanced across the animals to control for effects of the duration of stimulus exposure and of the passage of time itself (e.g., through variations in the level of anesthesia)

span.label: the omnibus ANOVA is used as a licence for the post-hoc comparisons rather than as the result, and the parametric choice is stated as forced
span.quote: As there were no suitable non-parametric alternatives, ANOVA for repeated measures with stimulus (standard, deviant) and time-segment (first, second, third) as factors was used to justify post-hoc deviant-standard LFP amplitude comparisons for each time segment separately.

span.label: electrode positions are verified histologically after the fact and only confirmed placements enter the analysis, so the sample size differs by structure
span.quote: For the hippocampal recordings, the electrodes successfully implanted in the targeted areas were applied in the analysis (9 animals for the subiculum, 8 for the CA1 area, and 6 for the dentate gyrus, Figure 1 )

span.label: the baseline is taken from a window straddling tone onset, so that time zero is the moment of deviance rather than the moment of sound
span.quote: baseline corrected against the mean activity in the ±25 ms from tone onset and, hence in the 50-ms time window prior to duration deviance

span.label: the received dichotomy is attacked on three separate grounds — too little data, an independent hippocampal novelty mechanism, and existing animal evidence — rather than on the new result alone
span.quote: The MMN-hippocampus dissociation may, however, be premature for a number of reasons.

span.label: The paper cannot explain why mismatch responses were absent in two of the four timing conditions.
span.quote: Therefore, why mismatch responses were absent precisely in the SSI 200 /SDI 200 - and SSI 500 /SDI 500 -conditions remains to be accounted for.

span.label: Deviant rarity as such, rather than change detection, remains a viable alternative explanation of the responses.
span.quote: Nevertheless, the rarity of the deviant tone as such [26] , [27] also remains a possible explanation for our findings.

span.label: The design lacked deviant-alone and equal-probability control conditions needed to test the change-detection account.
span.quote: Future studies with appropriate control procedures, such as deviant-alone (e.g. [18] ) or equal-probability (e.g. [19] ) stimulus conditions, are needed to test the validity of the change-detection account.

span.label: Whether the cortical and hippocampal responses share one mechanism, or reflect separate ones, is unresolved.
span.quote: It remains to be resolved whether these responses of different anatomical origins recruit a single but spatially distributed neural mechanism, spatially separate and independent neural mechanisms, or spatially separate but interconnected neural mechanisms.

span.label: three of the four stimulus conditions produced nothing
span.quote: In the remaining three conditions, the findings were negative.

span.label: why the two matched-interval conditions failed is left unexplained, and the explanations offered are labelled tentative
span.quote: Therefore, why mismatch responses were absent precisely in the SSI 200 /SDI 200 - and SSI 500 /SDI 500 -conditions remains to be accounted for.

span.label: the change-detection interpretation is not established by this design — mere rarity remains available
span.quote: Nevertheless, the rarity of the deviant tone as such [26] , [27] also remains a possible explanation for our findings.

span.label: the controls that would settle it were not run
span.quote: Future studies with appropriate control procedures, such as deviant-alone (e.g. [18] ) or equal-probability (e.g. [19] ) stimulus conditions, are needed to test the validity of the change-detection account.

span.label: whether the cortical and hippocampal responses are one mechanism, two independent ones, or two connected ones is undetermined
span.quote: It remains to be resolved whether these responses of different anatomical origins recruit a single but spatially distributed neural mechanism, spatially separate and independent neural mechanisms, or spatially separate but interconnected neural mechanisms.

span.label: the conditions differ in stimulus assignment and in sweep count as well as in interval, so the comparison across them is not clean
span.quote: In the SSI 200 /SDI 200 - and SSI 500 /SDI 500 -conditions, the stimulus assignments (the 25-ms tone as the deviant tone and the 75-ms tone as the standard tone, but not vice versa) and numbers (a half) of sweeps per averaged waveform were different from those in the SSI 500 /SDI 200 - and SSI 200 /SDI 500 -conditions.

span.label: the deviant differed from the standard on two features rather than one in the conditions that worked, which is itself a candidate explanation of the result
span.quote: The present pattern of observations may also reflect the fact that the deviant tone was distinguishable from the standard tone by two auditory features (tone duration and inter-stimulus interval) in the former pair of conditions as opposed to solely one feature (tone duration) in the latter pair [1] , [47] .

span.label: the pairwise comparisons carry no correction for multiple testing, and this is stated in the figure legend
span.quote: * P <0.05 and ** P <0.01 in post-hoc uncorrected comparisons (paired t-tests).

span.label: the entire oddball paradigm and the deviant-minus-standard subtraction logic, carried into rodent local field potentials with the polarity requirement dropped
span.quote: MMN is quantified by arithmetically subtracting ERPs to the standard tone from ERPs to the deviant tone.

span.label: the MMN-then-P3a sequence, imported as the prediction the animal data would have to match if the hippocampal response were merely downstream
span.quote: This would be analogous to a MMN-P3a sequence in humans that is only observable in full (i.e., also including P3a) when deviant tones of high magnitude attract involuntary switches of attention [1] , [4] .

span.label: the sequential order of the six stimulus series COUNTERBALANCED ACROSS ANIMALS
span.quote: was counterbalanced across the animals to control for effects of the duration of stimulus exposure and of the passage of time itself (e.g., through variations in the level of anesthesia)

span.label: mismatch negativity versus mismatch response — the human concept requires negative polarity by name; the animal concept is defined to ignore polarity, and here that difference is load-bearing
span.quote: Mismatch responses (i.e., higher-amplitude brain responses to deviant tones than standard tones irrespectively of the polarity of these responses and despite these tones are only passively listened to) have been found in sleeping infants [9] – [11] and in awake, sleeping and anesthetized animals [12] – [23]

span.label: deviance as a change in the standard, versus deviance as mere rarity — two accounts the design cannot separate
span.quote: Nevertheless, the rarity of the deviant tone as such [26] , [27] also remains a possible explanation for our findings.

span.label: time zero — from tone onset versus from the moment of duration change, which fall 25 ms apart and are distinguished throughout the results
span.quote: The zero time point is at the moment of change, that is, at 25 ms from tone onset and, thus, at the offset of the 25-ms tone.

span.label: deviance as a lengthening versus a shortening of the standard; the two are not equivalent, and only the working conditions included a lengthening
span.quote: Mismatch responses in rats have been found to be higher in amplitude to deviant tones as lengthenings than shortenings of standard tones [21] .

span.label: change detection versus stimulus-specific adaptation — a response reduction that is feature-specific, held to be a functionally different thing from a mismatch response
span.quote: Stimulus-specific adaptation, a decrease in neural responses to a repeated tone which is specific to the physical features of this tone, observed in different stages of the auditory pathway [48] – [51] as functionally distinct from auditory cortical mismatch responses [52] , [53] could provide a useful neurophysiological tool to increase this understanding.

span.label: hippocampal response as initial detection versus as a downstream consequence of cortical detection — the two readings the latency correspondence is meant to decide between
span.quote: Nevertheless, hippocampal mismatch responses could be claimed to be secondary to and solely triggered by auditory cortical mismatch responses in a limited set of circumstances.

span.label: critiques → the received cortico-hippocampal dichotomy in which the hippocampus contributes to P3a but not to MMN
span.quote: The MMN-hippocampus dissociation may, however, be premature for a number of reasons.

span.label: contradicts → intracranial human studies reporting no hippocampal mismatch responses, or only longer-latency novelty responses
span.quote: Studies employing intracranial hippocampal recordings in neurological patients have reported no mismatch responses [33] or other, longer-latency differential responses to deviant tones as novel or salient stimuli rather than as changes in standards [34] .

span.label: replicates → previous cortical mismatch findings in urethane-anesthetized rats, in polarity and latency
span.quote: The polarity and latency range of auditory cortical mismatch responses in the SSI 500 /SDI 200 -condition correspond to previous findings in urethane anesthetized rats [18] , [19] , [22] , [23] .

span.label: extends → animal work already reporting hippocampal mismatch responses, some of them specific to change rather than rarity
span.quote: Finally, hippocampal mismatch responses have been observed in animals [14] , [16] , and some of these responses have, comparably to MMN [3] , even shown specificity to deviant tones as changes in standard tones [16] .

span.label: builds-on → the proposal that the hippocampus responds to rare stimuli by comparison against a model of past repetition
span.quote: Second, the hippocampus has been proposed, comparably to MMN [1] , to respond by itself to rare stimuli on the basis of their discrepancy from a neural model of past repetitive stimuli [35] – [38] .

span.label: critiques → the state of MMN generator theory generally, as contested and unresolved
span.quote: The generators of MMN are largely unknown. Different and partially contradictory explanations have been proposed [8] , [26] – [28] .

span.label: mismatch negativity —distinct-from→ P3a
span.quote: The hippocampus is associated with a later generated P3a of ERPs reflecting involuntarily attention switches towards auditory changes that are high in magnitude.

span.label: mismatch negativity —operationalised-as→ preattentive
span.quote: In humans, the preattentive detection of auditory changes is indexed by an electrical brain response with a fronto-central scalp distribution termed the mismatch negativity (MMN) of event-related potentials (ERPs) [1] – [3] .

span.label: mismatch negativity —operationalised-as→ oddball condition
span.quote: MMN is typically experimentally addressed by using the so-called oddball condition.

span.label: deviant —contrasted-with→ standard
span.quote: In this condition, a (‘deviant’) tone rarely replaces a frequently repeated (‘standard’) tone.

span.label: memory trace —causes→ mismatch negativity
span.quote: MMN is elicited by the deviant tone only if the distinguishing feature(s) of the standard relative to the deviant are successfully represented neurally, stored in transient auditory memory, and compared to the auditory input by the deviant [1] , [7] , [8] .

span.label: stimulus-specific adaptation —distinct-from→ mismatch responses
span.quote: Stimulus-specific adaptation, a decrease in neural responses to a repeated tone which is specific to the physical features of this tone, observed in different stages of the auditory pathway [48] – [51] as functionally distinct from auditory cortical mismatch responses [52] , [53] could provide a useful neurophysiological tool to increase this understanding.

span.label: CA1 —part-of→ hippocampal system
span.quote: auditory cortical and hippocampal-system (CA1, dentate gyrus, subiculum) local-field potentials were recorded in urethane-anesthetized rats

span.label: P3a —operationalised-as→ involuntary attention
span.quote: If the auditory changes are of high magnitude, they can capture involuntary attention [4] and elicit a partly hippocampally-contributed P3a of ERPs in the later latency range of 250–280 ms [1] , [5] , [6] .

span.label: mismatch responses —operationalised-as→ local-field potentials
span.quote: We found differential LFPs (mismatch responses) to duration deviant tones in the auditory cortex and in the hippocampal system (CA1, dentate gyrus, and subiculum) in urethane-anesthetized rats.

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: As there were no suitable non-parametric alternatives, ANOVA for repeated measures with stimulus (standard, deviant) and time-segment (first, second, third) as factors was used to justify post-hoc deviant-standard LFP amplitude comparisons for each time segment separately.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Pairwise deviant-standard comparison for each time segment was made using the paired t test (two-tailed).

span.label: Greenhouse-Geisser correction
span.quote: Degrees of freedom were Greenhouse-Geisser corrected whenever the sphericity assumption was violated, and corrected P values were reported.

span.label: significance level
span.quote: An alpha level of 0.05 was used in all analyses.

span.label: p-value
span.quote: Post-hoc pairwise comparisons further indicated that this displacement was present (P<0.05) in the first time-segment (51.5–89 ms from duration change).

span.label: ANOVA for repeated measures
span.quote: ANOVA for repeated measures with stimulus (standard, deviant) and time-segment (first, second, third) as factors was used to justify post-hoc deviant-standard LFP amplitude comparisons for each time segment separately

span.label: Greenhouse-Geisser
span.quote: Degrees of freedom were Greenhouse-Geisser corrected whenever the sphericity assumption was violated, and corrected P values were reported.

span.label: paired t test (two-tailed)
span.quote: Pairwise deviant-standard comparison for each time segment was made using the paired t test (two-tailed).

span.label: alpha level of 0.05
span.quote: An alpha level of 0.05 was used in all analyses.

span.label: post-hoc uncorrected comparisons
span.quote: * P <0.05 and ** P <0.01 in post-hoc uncorrected comparisons (paired t-tests).

span.label: stimulus×time-segment -interaction
span.quote: as reflected by a significant stimulus×time-segment -interaction, F(2,14) = 11.34, P = 0.010

span.label: Mismatch responses to duration deviants were recorded not only in the auditory cortex but simultaneously in all three hippocampal-system sites (CA1, dentate gyrus and subiculum) of urethane-anesthetized rats.
span.quote: We found differential LFPs (mismatch responses) to duration deviant tones in the auditory cortex and in the hippocampal system (CA1, dentate gyrus, and subiculum) in urethane-anesthetized rats.

span.label: The cortical and hippocampal responses had opposite polarity (positive in cortex, negative in hippocampus) yet occupied the same 51.5-89 ms post-change latency window and appeared only in the condition combining a 500-ms standard-to-standard interval with a 200-ms standard-to-deviant interval.
span.quote: The responses - positive polarity in the auditory cortical and negative polarity in the hippocampal sites - appeared in the same latency range (between 51.5 and 89 ms post-change) and in all the recording sites, but only in the SSI 500 /SDI 200 -condition.

span.label: Of the four interval combinations tested, only the 500-ms SSI paired with the 200-ms SDI elicited mismatch responses; the other three combinations elicited none.
span.quote: Mismatch responses were observed at 51.5–89 ms with the 500-ms SSI coupled with the 200-ms SDI but not with the three remaining combinations.

span.label: Because the hippocampal responses coincided with the cortical ones in both latency and stimulus condition, the hippocampal activity reflects the initial detection of the deviant rather than a later, attention-switch stage.
span.quote: Most importantly, hippocampal and auditory cortical mismatch responses were found in the same latency range and in the same stimulus condition.

span.label: The authors conclude that the hippocampus may contribute to the cortical manifestation of the mismatch negativity, contradicting the assumed cortico-hippocampal dichotomy.
span.quote: The findings suggest that the hippocampus may play a role in (cortical) manifestation of MMN.

span.label: mismatch responses appeared in auditory cortex and all three hippocampal sites, at 51.5–89 ms post-change, but only in one of four conditions
span.quote: Mismatch responses were observed at 51.5–89 ms with the 500-ms SSI coupled with the 200-ms SDI but not with the three remaining combinations.

span.label: the cortical response was positive-going and the hippocampal responses negative-going, in the same animals and the same window
span.quote: The responses - positive polarity in the auditory cortical and negative polarity in the hippocampal sites - appeared in the same latency range (between 51.5 and 89 ms post-change) and in all the recording sites, but only in the SSI 500 /SDI 200 -condition.

span.label: in auditory cortex the effect was a stimulus by time-segment interaction, present in the first segment only
span.quote: as reflected by a stimulus (deviant tone, standard tone)×time-segment (first, second, third) -interaction, in the SSI 500/ SDI 200 condition, F(2,18) = 5.13, P = 0.048

span.label: in CA1 the effect was larger and lasted two segments rather than one
span.quote: Post-hoc pairwise comparisons further indicated that, in this condition, the displacement was present (P<0.05) in the first time segment (51.5–89 ms from duration change, P<0.001) and in the second time segment (89.5–127 ms from duration change, P<0.05).

span.label: dentate gyrus and subiculum showed the same first-segment displacement as CA1
span.quote: Furthermore, as in the CA1 and DG, the LFPs in the subiculum were displaced towards negative polarity in response to the deviant tone relative to the standard tone, as reflected by a significant stimulus×time-segment -interaction, F(2,16) = 8.18, P = 0.017, in the SSI 500/ SDI 200 condition.

span.label: no main effect of stimulus in auditory cortex in any condition
span.quote: No main effect of stimulus was present in any condition (P≥0.211).

span.label: the tone-evoked waveform itself peaked at about 40 ms in cortex and had two negative peaks at about 20 and 40 ms in hippocampus, both timed from tone onset rather than from deviance
span.quote: In the CA1 area of the hippocampus, the tones evoked a two-peaked negative deflection, the first peak occurring at about 20 ms and the second at about 40 ms from stimulus onset (i.e., not from deviance which occurred at 25 ms after stimulus onset).

span.label: in dentate gyrus one further condition gave a significant interaction that post-hoc testing reduced to a trend in the last segment
span.quote: However, post-hoc comparisons only showed a trend for the deviant-standard difference in the last (127.5 ms −165 ms) time segment (P = 0.09).

span.label: usable electrodes differed by structure: 9 animals for subiculum, 8 for CA1, 6 for dentate gyrus
span.quote: For the hippocampal recordings, the electrodes successfully implanted in the targeted areas were applied in the analysis (9 animals for the subiculum, 8 for the CA1 area, and 6 for the dentate gyrus, Figure 1 )

span.label: sweep retention was high — never below 67 of 100, averaging 98.7
span.quote: Not less than 67 out of 100 sweeps were included in calculating the average values per stimulus type and condition in any animal, the average number being 98.7 out of 100 sweeps.

span.label: mismatch negativity (MMN)
span.quote: In humans, the preattentive detection of auditory changes is indexed by an electrical brain response with a fronto-central scalp distribution termed the mismatch negativity (MMN) of event-related potentials (ERPs)

span.label: mismatch responses
span.quote: Mismatch responses (i.e., higher-amplitude brain responses to deviant tones than standard tones irrespectively of the polarity of these responses and despite these tones are only passively listened to) have been found in sleeping infants

span.label: oddball condition
span.quote: In this condition, a (‘deviant’) tone rarely replaces a frequently repeated (‘standard’) tone.

span.label: stimulus-specific adaptation
span.quote: Stimulus-specific adaptation, a decrease in neural responses to a repeated tone which is specific to the physical features of this tone, observed in different stages of the auditory pathway

span.label: Mismatch responses
span.quote: Mismatch responses (i.e., higher-amplitude brain responses to deviant tones than standard tones irrespectively of the polarity of these responses and despite these tones are only passively listened to)

span.label: oddball condition
span.quote: In this condition, a (‘deviant’) tone rarely replaces a frequently repeated (‘standard’) tone.

span.label: MMN
span.quote: MMN is quantified by arithmetically subtracting ERPs to the standard tone from ERPs to the deviant tone.

span.label: Stimulus-specific adaptation
span.quote: Stimulus-specific adaptation, a decrease in neural responses to a repeated tone which is specific to the physical features of this tone

span.label: P3a
span.quote: The hippocampus is associated with a later generated P3a of ERPs reflecting involuntarily attention switches towards auditory changes that are high in magnitude.

span.label: stimulus type (rare duration deviant vs. repeated standard tone)
span.term: stimulus type (rare duration deviant vs. repeated standard tone)
span.quote: A rare tone in duration (deviant) was interspersed with a repeated tone (standard).

span.label: standard-to-standard and standard-to-deviant intervals (200 ms vs. 500 ms)
span.term: standard-to-standard and standard-to-deviant intervals (200 ms vs. 500 ms)
span.quote: Two standard-to-standard (SSI) and standard-to-deviant (SDI) intervals (200 ms vs. 500 ms) were applied in different combinations to vary the observability of responses resembling MMN (mismatch responses).

span.label: mean local-field-potential amplitude in successive 37.5-ms post-stimulus segments
span.term: mean local-field-potential amplitude in successive 37.5-ms post-stimulus segments
span.quote: From these averaged LFP waveforms, the mean amplitudes of three consecutive post-stimulus 37.5-ms time segments were calculated from 51.5 ms post-change (76.5 ms post-stimulus) onwards

span.label: sound frequency (deliberately not varied, to avoid a refractoriness confound)
span.term: sound frequency (deliberately not varied, to avoid a refractoriness confound)
span.quote: Sound frequency was not used due to its spatial coding from the cochlea [41] owing to a potential confounding effect of lower levels of refractoriness in afferent pathways activated by the rare deviant tone than the frequently occurring standard tones [1] .

span.label: order of the six stimulus series (counterbalanced across animals)
span.term: order of the six stimulus series (counterbalanced across animals)
span.quote: was counterbalanced across the animals to control for effects of the duration of stimulus exposure and of the passage of time itself (e.g., through variations in the level of anesthesia).

span.label: stimulus (standard, deviant)
span.quote: ANOVA for repeated measures with stimulus (standard, deviant) and time-segment (first, second, third) as factors

span.label: time-segment
span.quote: the mean amplitudes of three consecutive post-stimulus 37.5-ms time segments were calculated from 51.5 ms post-change (76.5 ms post-stimulus) onwards

span.label: SSI
span.quote: Otherwise, the four conditions differed in stimulus-onset-asynchrony (200 ms or 500 ms) between consecutive standards (SSI) and between deviants and their immediately preceding standards (SDI).

span.label: response amplitude
span.quote: Significant differences in response amplitude between the deviant and the standard are marked between the curves.

span.label: brain location
span.quote: We averaged the LFPs for each stimulus type (the deviant tone and the standard tone which immediately preceded the deviant tone) in each brain location, stimulus condition ( Figure 2 ), and animal.

span.label: 51.5–89 ms — latency window after the duration change in which mismatch responses appeared at every recording site
span.quote: Mismatch responses were observed at 51.5–89 ms with the 500-ms SSI coupled with the 200-ms SDI but not with the three remaining combinations.

span.label: Ten — number of rats used, weighing 305-375 g
span.quote: Ten Spraque Dawley rats were used in the experiment (weight 305–375 g).

span.label: 1000 — number of tones in each stimulus series, with consecutive deviants separated by at least two standards
span.quote: occurred in a series of 1000 tones randomly with the restriction that consecutive deviants were separated by at least two standards.

span.label: 25 vs. 75 ms — the duration difference between deviant and standard tone that constituted the deviance
span.quote: The deviant tone differed from the standard tone in duration (25 vs. 75 ms).

span.label: 4000-Hz — frequency of the sinusoidal tones, held identical for deviant and standard
span.quote: Sinusoidal 4000-Hz tones of 25 ms and 75 ms in duration, including 5-ms rise and fall times, were used as stimuli.

span.label: 98.7 out of 100 — average number of artifact-free sweeps entering each averaged waveform
span.quote: Not less than 67 out of 100 sweeps were included in calculating the average values per stimulus type and condition in any animal, the average number being 98.7 out of 100 sweeps.

span.label: 9 ... 8 ... 6 — number of animals with usable electrodes in subiculum, CA1 and dentate gyrus respectively
span.quote: For the hippocampal recordings, the electrodes successfully implanted in the targeted areas were applied in the analysis (9 animals for the subiculum, 8 for the CA1 area, and 6 for the dentate gyrus, Figure 1 ).

span.label: 51.5–89 ms — the post-change window in which mismatch responses appeared at every site
span.quote: Mismatch responses were observed at 51.5–89 ms with the 500-ms SSI coupled with the 200-ms SDI but not with the three remaining combinations.

span.label: 25 vs 75 ms — the two tone durations serving as deviant and standard
span.quote: The deviant tone differed from the standard tone in duration (25 vs. 75 ms).

span.label: 200 ms vs. 500 ms — the two interval values crossed to make the four conditions
span.quote: Two standard-to-standard (SSI) and standard-to-deviant (SDI) intervals (200 ms vs. 500 ms) were applied in different combinations

span.label: P = 0.1 and P = 0.9 — deviant and standard probabilities in a series of 1000 tones
span.quote: The deviant (P = 0.1) and the standard (P = 0.9) occurred in a series of 1000 tones randomly with the restriction that consecutive deviants were separated by at least two standards.

span.label: ten rats — the sample, 305–375 g
span.quote: Ten Spraque Dawley rats were used in the experiment (weight 305–375 g).

span.label: 1.2 g/kg — urethane dose, topped up by pedal withdrawal reflex
span.quote: The animals were anaesthetized with urethane (Sigma-Aldrich, St. Louis, MO, USA) i.p. (1.2 g/kg).

span.label: 4000-Hz, 70 dB — tone frequency and sound pressure level
span.quote: Sinusoidal 4000-Hz tones of 25 ms and 75 ms in duration, including 5-ms rise and fall times, were used as stimuli.

span.label: 37.5-ms segments — the analysis window width, three of five used, starting 50 ms from change
span.quote: For the response amplitude analysis, the response time of 187.5 ms, as calculated from tone onset, was divided into five 37.5-ms segments.

span.label: 150–250 ms — the human MMN latency range
span.quote: MMN can be elicited in the latency range of 150–250 ms even by changes perceptually too weak to attract involuntary attention [1] .
